## Why MAST and pseudobulk DESeq2 return near-disjoint DEG sets {#sec-overview}

This note explains why the MAST and pseudobulk DESeq2 workflows in
`scripts/06_02_MAST_biological_exploration_transcriptomic_differential_analyses.R`
and `scripts/06_02_deseq2_biological_exploration_transcriptomic_differential_analyses.R`
return largely non-overlapping differentially expressed gene (DEG) sets, as
summarised in the Venn comparison (`scripts/06_02_compare_DEGs.R`).

### Notation and indices {#sec-notation}

Both frameworks are fitted **per Luque cell type** $t$, but they define
different experimental units and responses (@tbl-notation). All equations below
use this shared notation.

| Symbol | Role | MAST | DESeq2 pseudobulk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $g$ | Gene index | Tested gene | Tested gene |
| $i$ | Single-cell index | **Experimental unit** | Aggregated into pseudobulk |
| $s$ | Organoid (`Sample.barcode`) | Implicit via $s(i)$ | **Experimental unit** |
| $t$ | Luque cell type | Separate model per $t$ | Separate pseudobulk per $t$ |
| $k_{gi}$, $Y_{gi}$ | Raw count / normalised expression of gene $g$ in cell $i$ | Model response (log-normalised layer) | Summed to $K_{gst}$ |
| $K_{gst}$ | Pseudobulk count for $(g,s,t)$ | Not used | Model response |
| $z_{gi}=\mathbf{1}(Y_{gi}>0)$ | Detection indicator | Bernoulli (D) component | Absorbed in sum |
| $x_s$ | Morphotype of organoid $s$ | Fixed effect via $x_i=x_{s(i)}$ | Fixed effect |
| $\text{cngeneson}_i$ | Scaled cellular detection rate (CDR) | Nuisance covariate | Not used |
| $S_{st}$ | Size factor for $(s,t)$ | Not used | Library-size normaliser |
| $\beta_{g,\mathrm{Morph}}$ | Morphotype coefficient | Primary estimand | Primary estimand |
| $\phi_g$ | Gene-wise dispersion | Not used | NB overdispersion |
| $n_{st}$ | Cells in cell type $t$, organoid $s$ | — | Used in averaging |
| $m$ | Number of tested genes | ~11,352 (neural) | ~11,352 (neural) |
| $q$ | FDR target | 0.05 | 0.05 |

: Homogenised indices and variables in the MAST and DESeq2 workflows {#tbl-notation}

Counts are first aggregated within each cell type and organoid:

$$
K_{gst} = \sum_{i \in (s,t)} k_{gi}
$$ {#eq-pseudobulk-sum}

DESeq2 then models $K_{gst}$; MAST models $Y_{gi}$ and $z_{gi}$ directly and
does not use @eq-pseudobulk-sum.

### The fundamental mismatch: statistical unit of inference {#sec-unit}

The root cause is that the two frameworks define the **experimental unit**
differently (@tbl-statistical-unit, @tbl-notation).

| Framework | Statistical unit | $n$ (neural, per group) |
|-----------|-----------------|--------------------------|
| Pseudobulk DESeq2 | Organoid (sample barcode) | 12 |
| MAST (current implementation) | Cell | ~3,700–3,800 |

: Statistical unit and effective sample size for the neural cell type {#tbl-statistical-unit}

Crowell et al. term this the distinction between *cell-level* and
*sample-level* inference. They write explicitly:

> *"Most current scRNA-seq differential expression methods are designed to test
> one set of cells against another … In such statistical models, the cells are
> the experimental units … [but] the goal shifts to making sample-level
> inferences (i.e., experimental units are samples), in order to account for
> sample-to-sample as well as cell-to-cell variability."*

The MAST hurdle model fitted per cell type $t$ is:

$$
\underbrace{\text{logit}\,P(Y_{gi} > 0)}_{\text{discrete (D)}} = \alpha_g^D + \beta_{g,\mathrm{Morph}}^D\,x_i + \beta_{g,\mathrm{cdr}}^D\,\text{cngeneson}_i
$$ {#eq-mast-discrete}

$$
\underbrace{E[Y_{gi} \mid Y_{gi} > 0]}_{\text{continuous (C)}} = \alpha_g^C + \beta_{g,\mathrm{Morph}}^C\,x_i + \beta_{g,\mathrm{cdr}}^C\,\text{cngeneson}_i
$$ {#eq-mast-continuous}

where $i$ indexes **cells** (~7,479 for neural). No random effect for
`Sample.barcode` is included (`formula = ~ Morphotype + cngeneson`,
`method = "glm"`). Cells from the same organoid are therefore treated as
independent biological replicates — a form of **pseudoreplication**.

The DESeq2 model works on @eq-pseudobulk-sum and tests:

$$
K_{gst} \sim \text{NB}(\mu_{gst},\,\phi_g), \quad \log\mu_{gst} = \beta_{g0t} + \beta_{gt,\mathrm{Morph}}\,x_s + \log S_{st}
$$ {#eq-deseq2-nb}

where $s$ indexes **organoids** (12 per group). The likelihood-ratio test (LRT)
compares $\sim\text{Morphotype}$ vs $\sim 1$, with $\sim 22$ effective degrees
of freedom.

Together, @eq-mast-discrete, @eq-mast-continuous, and @eq-deseq2-nb formalise
the core design difference: MAST conditions on cell-level covariates and treats
cells as replicates, whereas DESeq2 models organoid-level count variation after
pseudobulk aggregation.

### Artificial inflation of statistical power in MAST {#sec-power}

The hurdle LRT statistic is:

$$
\Lambda = 2\bigl[\ell(\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_{\text{full}}) - \ell(\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_{\text{reduced}})\bigr] \xrightarrow{H_0} \chi^2_1
$$ {#eq-mast-lrt}

Under standard regression, power scales with $\sqrt{n}$. When
$n = n_{\text{cells}} \approx 7{,}479$ rather than $n = n_{\text{samples}} = 24$,
the effective standard error of $\hat\beta_{g,\mathrm{Morph}}$ shrinks by roughly
$\sqrt{7{,}479 / 24} \approx 18$-fold. Biological noise shared across cells
within the same organoid is treated as independent signal, inflating $\Lambda$
in @eq-mast-lrt and producing very small p-values for effects invisible with
sample-level replication. Crowell et al. demonstrate (Fig. 3):

> *"Most isolated intersections, i.e., hits unique to a certain method, were
> genes that had been stimulated to be EE [equally expressed] and thus false
> discoveries … AD, MAST, and scDD methods report large numbers of isolated
> hits"*

The Venn results are consistent with this: MAST returns 41 FDR-significant DEGs
in neural cells; DESeq2 returns 0. The 41 MAST-specific hits match the expected
pattern of inflated false positives from pseudoreplication.

### Why DESeq2 returns no FDR-significant DEGs after correction {#sec-fdr}

With 12 vs 12 organoids and $m \approx 11{,}352$ tested genes, the
Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) threshold for the $k$-th ranked p-value is:

$$
p_{(k)} \leq \frac{k}{m}\,q = \frac{k}{11{,}352} \times 0.05
$$ {#eq-bh-threshold}

The data show 575 genes with raw $p < 0.05$ in neural, but the minimum
adjusted p-value is 0.133. The raw p-value distribution is only weakly enriched
below 0.05 — consistent with a real but weak signal **below the power
resolution** of 12 biological replicates. For a gene to survive BH at position
$k = 1$, @eq-bh-threshold requires:

$$
p_{\min} \leq \frac{1}{11{,}352} \times 0.05 \approx 4.4 \times 10^{-6}
$$ {#eq-bh-min}

The observed minimum raw p-value is $\approx 9.8 \times 10^{-6}$, just above
the bound in @eq-bh-min. DESeq2 is not failing to detect biology; it correctly
acknowledges that 12 organoids cannot separate signal from noise at genome-wide
FDR 5% given the effect sizes present.

### Different model assumptions and input data {#sec-assumptions}

Beyond replication, the workflows differ in likelihood, input scale, and
covariate handling (@tbl-model-comparison).

| Aspect | MAST | DESeq2 pseudobulk |
|--------|------|-------------------|
| Input data | Log-normalised expression (`data` layer) | Raw integer counts |
| Distribution | Zero-inflated hurdle GLM (logistic + Gaussian/GLM) | Negative binomial |
| LFC scale | $\log_e$ of log-normalised values | $\log_2$ fold-change on count scale |
| Per-cell covariate | `cngeneson` (scaled CDR) | None |
| Shrinkage | None (`ebayes = FALSE`) | DESeq2 MAP shrinkage (LRT here) |

: Comparison of MAST and pseudobulk DESeq2 modelling assumptions {#tbl-model-comparison}

The `cngeneson` covariate absorbs sequencing-depth variation at the cell level:

$$
\text{cngeneson}_i = \frac{\text{n\_detected}_i - \overline{\text{n\_detected}}}{\text{SD}(\text{n\_detected})}
$$ {#eq-cngeneson}

If cells from `neural_bias` organoids have systematically higher CDR, its
coefficient in @eq-mast-discrete and @eq-mast-continuous may absorb
transcriptome-wide morphotype differences, or partially remove capture-efficiency
confounding. DESeq2 handles depth through $S_{st}$ in @eq-deseq2-nb at the
pseudobulk level only.

MAST therefore models detection and expression on a log-normalised, cell-level
scale, whereas DESeq2 models count overdispersion after @eq-pseudobulk-sum.
Crowell et al. (Supplementary Fig. 5) show that hurdle and mixed models on log
counts **systematically underestimate logFCs** compared with NB pseudobulk
methods on raw counts.

### Resolution of biological signal {#sec-resolution}

The statistical differences above also explain why downstream enrichment
profiles diverge between frameworks.

**DESeq2 captures organoid-level developmental programs.** Pseudobulk aggregation
averages over cells within each $(s,t)$ stratum:

$$
\bar{q}_{gt}^{(s)} = \frac{1}{n_{st}} \sum_{i \in (s,t)} q_{gi}
$$ {#eq-pseudobulk-mean}

Cell-to-cell stochasticity is suppressed; a pathway becomes significant only when
many genes shift coherently across organoids. This favours axial/regionalisation
programs, morphogen-response modules, and stable cell-type regulatory states.
Accordingly, DESeq2 enrichment emphasises **neural regionalisation** and
**somitic FGFR signalling** — large-scale tissue-patterning programs consistent
with axial organisation in the Villaronga-Luque gastruloid model.

**MAST captures fine-grained metabolic and signalling heterogeneity.** Via
@eq-mast-discrete, MAST can detect shifts in

$$
P(Y_{gi} > 0 \mid \text{neural\_bias}) \neq P(Y_{gi} > 0 \mid \text{TLS})
$$

even when @eq-pseudobulk-mean changes only weakly. It is sensitive to subpopulations
with stronger OXPHOS, somitic glucose/glycolysis activation, NMP gap-junction
turnover, and small retinoic-acid or junctional substates. MAST enrichment
accordingly highlights **OXPHOS/electron transport**, **glucose metabolism**,
**gap junctions**, **cadherin/adherens signalling**, and **retinoic acid** —
differences that may affect only a fraction of cells and are diluted by
@eq-pseudobulk-sum.

These biological contrasts are real hypotheses, but MAST-specific enrichment
must be weighed against the pseudoreplication caveat in @sec-power: without a
`(1 \mid \text{Sample.barcode})` random effect, thousands of dependent cells
inflate significance.

### Summary of contributing causes, ranked by importance {#sec-summary}

1. **Pseudoreplication (dominant effect).** MAST without a
   `(1 \mid \text{Sample.barcode})` random effect treats $n \approx 7{,}500$
   dependent cells as independent replicates, inflating the LRT in @eq-mast-lrt
   by a factor of $\sim n_{\text{cells}}/n_{\text{samples}} \approx 300$. This
   alone explains the large number of MAST-specific hits and the lack of overlap
   with DESeq2.

2. **Low biological replication in DESeq2.** With 12 organoids per group and
   ~11,000 genes, DESeq2 is correctly conservative: 575 genes pass raw
   $p < 0.05$, but none survive @eq-bh-threshold. The minimum padj of 0.133 is
   the honest answer given the data.

3. **Different resolution of biological signal.** @eq-pseudobulk-mean and
   @eq-deseq2-nb favour organoid-coherent patterning programs; @eq-mast-discrete
   and @eq-mast-continuous favour cell-state heterogeneity (@sec-resolution).

4. **Different likelihoods and input data.** MAST's hurdle GLM on log-normalised
   data and DESeq2's NB model on raw counts capture different aspects of
   expression variability (@tbl-model-comparison). LFCs are not on the same scale
   and are not expected to rank genes identically.

5. **`cngeneson` covariate.** MAST regresses out cellular CDR via @eq-cngeneson,
   modifying which genes appear significant relative to DESeq2.

### Interpretation and integrated biological model {#sec-interpretation}

**Statistical caution.** MAST results reflect largely cell-level variation
without organoid-to-organoid variability and should be treated cautiously. The
replication-aware estimate is DESeq2's: effect sizes are below what 12 organoids
can resolve at genome-wide FDR (@eq-bh-threshold, @eq-bh-min). The raw-$p$
overlap in the Venn comparison (4 genes at sample level, 3–4 at cell-type level)
is the most credible shared set.

**Integrated biological model.** The frameworks are nonetheless compatible with
the Villaronga-Luque model of early metabolic bias in NMPs shaping the fate
landscape:

1. **Original paper:** higher glycolysis supports TLS formation and mesodermal/somitic
   output; lower glycolysis and/or compensatory OXPHOS associates with neural-biased
   outcomes.
2. **DESeq2 (120 h):** early differences manifest as organoid-level programs. TLS
   retains stronger **neural regionalisation** and **somitic FGFR signalling**,
   consistent with better axial and paraxial-mesoderm patterning.
3. **MAST (120 h):** the same phenotype decomposes into finer cell states — neural
   OXPHOS/electron transport, somitic glucose/glycolysis, and junctional or
   retinoic-acid substates in NMP, pluripotent, and unknown compartments.

> Pseudo-bulk DESeq2 recovers the **tissue-level transcriptional consequences**
> of morphotype divergence — regionalisation and FGFR-associated somitic
> organisation — whereas MAST resolves **cell-state metabolic and signalling
> heterogeneity**, especially OXPHOS, glucose metabolism, and cell-cell
> communication. Both are compatible with metabolic imbalance preceding, and
> likely helping drive, the neural-biased versus TLS-like phenotypic landscape.

To increase DESeq2 power, options include more biological replicates or a model
that borrows strength across cell types (e.g.
[muscat](https://bioconductor.org/packages/muscat) with its `pbDS` wrapper around
edgeR/DESeq2 using shared dispersion).
